smells.finding: _compile_gate grew a spec_type branch (round 1: ~30 lines, round 2: ~60) but stays single-level branching (if/else on spec_type, one more if on is_last) with no nesting beyond that -- most of the added length is two literal dict/note constructions, not control flow. Not long-method by the shape that matters (branch depth / distinct responsibilities per branch), just a slightly longer function body.

CLAIM_ENFORCEMENT_GATED and CLAIM_ENFORCEMENT_SURVEY are two long, structurally-parallel prose constants (same shape: mechanism name, engine call, consequence). Considered as duplication and rejected: they are data, not logic, and their content is NOT parameterizable text -- one describes a real check that blocks, the other describes the absence of one and names a different engine call (record/consolidate vs advance) with different scoping words (command-kind vs no-filter). A shared template would need conditionals mirroring the very branch that already selects between them, adding indirection to save two string literals. Rule-of-two also applies (only these two instances exist).

large_claims widened from a 2-tuple (id, text) to a 3-tuple (id, text, enforcement), used in exactly one list comprehension (compile_spec) and unpacked in exactly one dict comprehension (_compile_gate's claims_rollup). A single local tuple threaded through two adjacent call sites in the same module is not the repeated, spreading clump the smell describes.

enforcement is one of exactly two fixed string constants (CLAIM_ENFORCEMENT_GATED / CLAIM_ENFORCEMENT_SURVEY), matching the repo's existing convention for closed string vocabularies (CHECK_KINDS, RESERVED_CONDITION_ID) rather than introducing a new stringly-typed field that needed a real type.

_compile_gate gained one keyword-only parameter (spec_type), now 4 keyword-only args (hand_back_to, is_last, large_claims, spec_type) plus the positional gate dict -- still enumerable at a glance, no parameter-object pressure yet.

The fix touches scripts/generate_spine.py (source) and tests/test_generate_spine.py (tests) for one conceptual change (make survey-side enforcement honest) -- expected source+test coupling, not scatter. specs/*.toml were correctly left untouched (enforcement is fully generator-computed from spec.type, not spec-authored), which is evidence AGAINST shotgun surgery: the fix did not have to ripple into the spec files at all.

Considered: _compile_gate already carries two concerns (Property 1's handback contract, Property 2's claim escalation) from round 1, and round 2 adds a third axis (spec_type) to the second concern rather than a new concern. This diff conditionalizes existing logic in place; it does not give _compile_gate a new reason to change beyond the one (Property 2's enforcement semantics) that motivated this entire rework. Not new divergent-change pressure introduced by this diff.

No new check kind, no new spec field, no raw-command escape. The branch is exactly the two cases DESIGN_NOTE.md section 6's correction names (gated vs survey) -- nothing generalized beyond what is instantiated by the two shipped role specs.

New comments on CLAIM_ENFORCEMENT_GATED/SURVEY and the two _compile_gate branches state non-obvious WHY (which engine verb consults which postcondition kind, ticket refs #422/#328, the round-2 rework's own rationale) rather than restating what the following line does -- the case where a comment earns its place per CREW_CONTEXT.md's verification-discipline section.
